title: GOP’s Corporate Funders Target Minnesota Attorney General
author: Claire Kelloway
content:

Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison is running for a third term against
Republican challenger Ron Schutz (not to be confused with his last opponent,
[Jim Schultz](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2022/09/28/voter-guide-see-
minnesota-attorney-general-candidates-stances)). While a Republican has [not
held the office in Minnesota since 1971](https://www.startribune.com/keep-an-
eye-on-the-minnesota-ags-race-for-2026/601231474), Ellison's last bid for re-
election was a [nail-
biter](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-elections/minnesota-attorney-
general-results/): He won 50.4% to 49.5% by just over 20,000 votes. This
year's contest is just as close; a [mid-September
poll](https://www.newsweek.com/republican-leads-minnesota-poll-democrats-seat-
decades-12454517) had Schutz slightly ahead with 45% of the likely vote to
Ellison's 43%.

Across the nation, elections for state attorneys general can be some of the
most consequential in shaping a state's posture toward the federal government,
which is [top of mind](https://fox59.com/news/national-world/minnesota-
democrats-lead-michelle-tafoya-mike-lindell-in-upcoming-elections/) for
Minnesotans in the wake of Operation Metro Surge.

State attorneys general are
[increasingly](https://attorneysgeneral.org/multistate-lawsuits-vs-the-
federal-government/) banding together to challenge federal law breaking,
including [illegal federal funding cuts](https://ag.ny.gov/press-
release/2026/attorney-general-james-wins-case-blocking-trump-administrations-
attacks) by the Trump administration. Bipartisan coalitions of state attorneys
general also serve as key cops on the beat in areas where federal enforcers
are stepping back, such as in antitrust, consumer protection, and
environmental protection.

But the office can play a harmful role as well. Since 1999, dark money and
special interest groups have funneled tens of millions of dollars toward the
[Republican Attorneys General Association](https://republicanags.com/) (RAGA).
RAGA has [been criticized](https://www.exposedbycmd.org/2026/10/23/elon-musk-
koch-and-big-tobacco-bankroll-republican-ags-group/) as a "pay to play"
organization helping elect GOP attorneys general to support corporate
interests and, in some cases, [undermine
democracy](https://www.propublica.org/article/raga-gop-jan6-amazon-walmart-
comcast-contributions). According to the Center for Media and Democracy, top
RAGA donors in 2026 include Elon Musk, OpenAI, Koch Industries, FanDuel (an
online prediction market and sportsbook), and Bayer (the chemical giant that
manufactures RoundUp).

Attorneys general are up for election in 30 states this year. According to
[The Center for
Politics](https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/democratic-outlook-
brightens-in-races-for-vital-state-ag-posts/) at the University of Virginia,
eight of these races are competitive, three of which lean Democrat (Wisconsin,
Nevada and Arizona), while three lean Republican (Kansas, Iowa and Georgia),
and two are toss-ups (Michigan and Minnesota).

## **Ellison 's Track Record**

During and after the influx of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
agents in 2025--not just in Minneapolis but in
[rural](https://prospect.org/2026/03/30/apr-2026-magazine-when-ice-blows-
through-rural-america-minnesota/)
[communities](https://www.foodandpower.net/latest/operation-metro-surge-
impact-on-rural-mn-meatpacking-towns-mar-26) [across the
state](https://www.startribune.com/with-ice-surge-spreading-across-state-
rumors-and-anxiety-grow-in-greater-minnesota/601562255)--Ellison sued the
federal government for [violating Minnesotans' constitutional
rights](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/72132615/state-of-minnesota-v-
noem/) and [withholding evidence from the state's
investigations](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/10/23/trump-administration-
stopped-sharing-evidence-in-good-pretti-killings-minnesota-officials-say) into
the killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti. Both cases are ongoing.

Ellison has a track record of fighting to protect Minnesotans against federal
and corporate bullying. Schutz claims he'll do the same, though like most
Minnesota Republicans this election cycle his campaign focuses a lot more on
fraud than challenging corporate power or the Trump administration.
Republicans are [hammering](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/republicans-
see-minnesota-fraud-scandal-as-a-chance-to-go-on-offense-in-a-blue-state)
Minnesota Democrats for failing to prevent hundreds of millions of dollars
stolen in [food, housing, and health
care](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/minnesota-fraud-schemes-what-we-know/)
[programs](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2025/10/22_EvergreenRecovery.asp)
over the past five years. As one of the only incumbents on the ballot, Ellison
is particularly vulnerable to this narrative.

Ellison was first elected attorney general in 2018, when he [gave up his safe
seat](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2018/06/08/politics-friday-kieth-ellison)
representing Minnesota's 5th Congressional District. [While in Congress,
he](https://www.naag.org/attorney-general/keith-ellison/) founded the House
Antitrust and Consumer Justice Caucuses. Ellison [told
](https://www.minnpost.com/politics-policy/2018/06/why-keith-ellison-leaving-
safe-seat-congress-make-risky-bid-minnesota-attorn/)_[Minn
Post](https://www.minnpost.com/politics-policy/2018/06/why-keith-ellison-
leaving-safe-seat-congress-make-risky-bid-minnesota-attorn/)_ at the time that
he believed he could do more to hold power to account and protect working
people as the state attorney general than as a member of Congress.

Over his past two terms, Ellison has defended Minnesotans against historic
injustices in the national spotlight, including convicting Minneapolis police
officer Derek Chauvin for killing George Floyd. Ellison also joined with other
state attorneys general in [80 lawsuits](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Rule-Of-
Law/Litigation/) to challenge Trump administration policies that threaten
birthright citizenship, gender-affirming care, voting rights, and public
programs. This includes challenging, and in some cases preventing, federal
funding freezes for critical programs supporting low-income families including
the [Supplemental Nutrition Assistance
Program](https://www.jurist.org/news/2026/02/us-federal-court-blocks-snap-
funding-cuts-over-states-refusal-to-share-recipient-data/) (SNAP),
[Medicaid](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/72353395/state-of-minnesota-v-
oz/), and [child care
funding](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2026/02/06_ACF_FundingFreeze.asp),
which rural communities depend on.

Ellison has [sued](https://www.startribune.com/ag-invites-minnesotans-
struggling-with-medical-debt-collections-to-share-their-stories/600298148)
[hospital
systems](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2025/03/14_MayoClinic.asp)
[for their debt collection practices](https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-
settlement-on-medical-debt-saves-hutchinson-health-patients-184000/600069199),
in one instance forgiving [$184,000 in medical
debt](https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-settlement-on-medical-debt-saves-
hutchinson-health-patients-184000/600069199) for patients of Hutchinson
Health, a rural hospital 60 miles west of the Twin Cities. Minnesota has also
joined multiple bipartisan, multi-state suits challenging [opioid
manufacturers](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/opioids/), [other drug
companies](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2026/07/17_Glenmark.asp),
[Ticketmaster](https://www.axios.com/2026/03/10/live-nation-ticketmaster-
state-antitrust),
[Amazon](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2023/09/26_Amazon.asp),
[Google](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2025/04/17_Google.asp),
and numerous other dominant corporations.

Minnesota and Illinois [were the first states to
join](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/01/ftc-states-
sue-deere-company-protect-farmers-unfair-corporate-tactics-high-repair-costs)
the Federal Trade Commission's lawsuit against John Deere's monopolization of
farm equipment repair. Minnesota also led the state coalition on the
Department of Justice's [lawsuit against
AgriStats](https://www.foodandpower.net/latest/doj-agristats-suit-
oct-23?rq=DOJ), a data-sharing corporation accused of facilitating price-
fixing by meatpackers. Since May, Minnesota has joined the feds in settling
both cases. While some [antitrust](https://www.thebignewsletter.com/p/youll-
own-nothing-and-be-happy-why)
[advocates](https://www.economicliberties.us/press-release/economic-liberties-
condemns-doj-for-dropping-agri-stats-meatpacking-cartel-case/) would have
preferred that these cases go to trial for [a chance at a stronger
remedy](https://www.foodandpower.net/latest/agri-stats-settlement-may-26), the
states likely pushed to improve both settlements.

This work has made Ellison a target for corporations. As of the latest public
reports from mid-September, dark money PACs had spent [a record $6.8
million](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-news/record-pac-money-flowing-to-
minnesota-attorney-general-race/) on attack ads against Ellison, far
surpassing the $1.8 million spent against Schutz. According to [public
filings](https://cfb.mn.gov/reports-and-data/viewers/campaign-finance/large-
contribution-notices/), one anti-Ellison PAC, Minnesotans for Justice, has
ties to the Minnesota Private Business Council, a political advocacy group
[representing](https://www.growthmn.com/here-s-what-jim-schultz-s-minnesota-
private-business-council-is-up-to/) Minnesota corporations including
countertop maker Cambria and beef processor Rosen's Diversified, led by
Ellison's last challenger, Jim Schultz. Ellison has benefited from $4.2
million in supportive outside PAC spending compared to just $423,000 spent
supporting Schutz.

"I'm extremely concerned about the harm that corporate consolidation and
monopolies are having on farmers and rural communities generally throughout
our state," Ellison said in a statement to Barn Raiser _._

## **Schutz Eyes an Upset**

Ellison's Achilles heel is public discontent over pandemic-era fraud scandals,
which [Republicans blame on Minnesota
Democrats](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/republicans-see-minnesota-
fraud-scandal-as-a-chance-to-go-on-offense-in-a-blue-state). Most notably, a
non-profit called Feeding Our Future stole [$250
million](https://apnews.com/article/feeding-our-future-pandemic-fraud-
trial-847f42be252ecd373c60125fd4fae6e9) from a public program meant to feed
children during the Covid-19 pandemic. While the ringleader of this scheme was
a white woman, the majority of convicted Feeding Our Future fraudsters are
[Somali Americans](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/26/us/minnesota-welfare-
fraud-scandal.html). PAC-funded attack ads against [Ellison and other
Minnesota Democrats](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/10/16/campaign-ads-
blame-fraud-violence-on-somali-minnesotans) emphasize this fact to vilify
Minnesota's Somali community and advance an "us-versus-them" narrative. Since
the Feeding Our Future scandal, the state has found fraud in other public
programs meant to provide addiction services, housing for people with
disabilities, services for children with autism, and home health care.

Different state agencies are responsible for identifying and challenging fraud
in different state and federal programs (in the case of Feeding Our Future,
the Minnesota Department of Education was technically responsible). Attorneys
general oversee Medicaid fraud, specifically, plus they [represent state
agencies in legal
disputes](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2022/09/26_FeedingOurFuture.asp).

Schutz, Ellison's challenger, [says](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-news/ag-
candidate-schutz-says-hes-ready-to-break-60-year-losing-streak-for-gop/) he
will do more to prevent fraud. He
[accuses](https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/keith-ellison-defends-fraud-
record-trump-lawsuits-in-tight-minnesota-attorney-general-
race/?intcid=CNR-02-0623) Ellison of accepting too many plea deals in fraud
cases. In a debate broadcast by Minnesota Public Radio (MPR), Schutz said he
would allocate more resources to prosecute fraud and refuse to enter into plea
agreements to bring more fraudsters to trial.

"For the vast majority of fraud cases that Keith Ellison's office has
prosecuted, almost no one goes to jail, almost no one ends up with a felony on
their record, and the fraudsters pay at most just pennies on the dollars of
what they've stolen," Schutz said in a statement to Barn Raiser _._

Ellison has maintained that his office [held the Feeding Our Future fraudsters
accountable](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2022/09/26_FeedingOurFuture.asp)
to the extent they had jurisdiction to, [increased
staff](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/10/21/keith-ellison-running-for-
minnesota-attorney-general-in-2026) to prosecute fraud in the future, won
[over
300](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2026/02/25_MedicaidFraud.asp)
Medicaid fraud convictions, and
[advocated](https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2026/02/25_MedicaidFraud.asp)
for state-level legislation to increase Medicaid fraud penalties and aid
enforcement (legislation that Schutz
[opposed](https://ronformnag.com/Release.html)). Ellison [defended
himself](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-news/in-minnesota-convicted-
fraudsters-often-end-up-with-no-felonies-on-their-records/) by saying that it
is the judge's decision, not the attorney general's, to determine if a crime
rises to a felony-level sentence. Ellison told Barn Raiser that he oversees a
top-performing Medicaid fraud unit, which ranked, on average, "fifth in fraud
convictions across the entire country over the last six years."

[Until recently](https://hoodline.com/2026/03/top-twin-cities-trial-star-
ditches-power-firm-to-take-on-keith-ellison/), Schutz was a partner at a
national law firm, [Robins Kaplan](https://www.robinskaplan.com/). He chaired
former Minnesota Gov. Tim Pawlenty's judicial selection commission and served
on the board of [the Center for the American
Experiment](https://www.americanexperiment.org/), a conservative Minnesota
think tank with [ties to the Koch brothers](https://www.desmog.com/center-
american-experiment/). The organization opposes [teachers'
unions](https://www.americanexperiment.org/news/?issue=unions) and [renewable
energy](https://www.americanexperiment.org/reports/shattered-green-dreams),
among other issues. In addition to fighting fraud, Schutz is
[campaigning](https://www.ronformnag.com/priorities.html) on familiar
conservative priorities such as combating crime, supporting law enforcement,
and barring trans athletes from girls' sports.

As a trial attorney, Schutz [specialized](https://www.lawdragon.com/lawyer-
limelights/2022-07-14-legends-limelight-ronald-j-schutz)
[in](https://tcbmag.com/notable/ronald-schutz/) litigating environmental
insurance conflicts and suing corporations for patent infringement. Schutz
[says](https://www.ronformnag.com/home.html) he will "bring that same fight to
protect Minnesota families and defend consumers." When asked by MPR about the
factors he'd consider for enforcing consumer protection laws or challenging
harmful business practices, Schutz was vague.

"If they committed wrongdoing and Minnesotans were harmed, the attorney
general should take action against that," he said.

Barn Raiser asked Schutz how he would support rural communities.

"I grew up on a dairy farm in Southwestern Minnesota near the small town of
Adrian," he said. "I understand rural communities. These are my people and
when I'm attorney general I will make sure that they are heard and their
issues addressed."

Ellison criticized Schutz for having [$1.74 million in personal stock
holdings](https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/09/29/minnesota-republican-ag-
candidates-stock-portfolio-presents-174-potential-conflicts-of-interest/) in
the very corporations he will be expected to prosecute. Schutz has
[promised](https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/10/02/at-ag-debate-republican-
ron-schutz-commits-to-putting-stocks-in-blind-trust/) that, if elected, he
will put his investments under blind management and divest holdings from
companies sued by the state.

When it comes to challenging the federal government, Schutz noted that he
called for a joint state and federal investigation into the shootings of Alex
Pretti and Renee Good. On MPR, Schutz said he has no problem suing the Trump
administration if they are "truly hurting Minnesotans." However, he dismissed
many of the multi-state cases brought against the federal government as
"political theatre." When asked by MPR if there was a specific case that
Minnesota joined that Schutz had a problem with, Schutz admitted that he has
not had the time to look at all of those cases.

Nearly 420,000 votes have been [cast in-person or by
mail](https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/in-person-early-voting-minnesota-
heres-what-to-know/) during the first five weeks of early voting. How
Minnesota responds to corporate power and an increasingly authoritarian
federal government now lies in the hands of its voters.

_Full disclosure: The author works for the Open Markets Institute, which has
provided subject area research to the Minnesota Attorney General 's Office and
spoken at their legal education events._
